# StackPreview

Namespace `Nfty.Core.Imaging` in assembly `Nfty.Core`.

```csharp
public static class StackPreview
```

Composites several layers at their real depths, so art authored one layer at a time can be lined up against the layers it will actually sit between.

**It introduces no third rendering path.** Every layer goes through `VariantPreview.Render` — the one rule for what a Variant looks like — and the stack goes through [`Compositor.Composite()`](Nfty.Core.Imaging.Compositor.md#m-composite-nfty-core-model-dimensions-system-collection-cb4a2f) — the one rule for how layers combine. That is the property the project protects: the CLI's `preview` and the GUI's preview must produce the *same* image, not a similar one, and two copies of a colorizer is precisely how that stops being true.

## Methods

### PickVariant(LoadedIngredient) { #m-pickvariant-nfty-core-formats-loadedingredient }

```csharp
public static string PickVariant(LoadedIngredient ingredient);
```

The variant to show when the caller has not named one: **highest weight, ties broken by ordinal-first id**.

Deliberately not a roll. A reference layer that changed appearance between repaints would make the alignment this feature exists to show unreadable, so there is no RNG here — and the tie-break is ordinal because a culture-sensitive one would pick differently on another machine.

A zero weight shelves a variant from generation but does not hide it here: the most probable variant is simply the one with the largest weight, and an ingredient whose variants are all shelved still previews as its ordinal-first one rather than failing.

**Parameters**

- `ingredient` (`LoadedIngredient`) - The layer to pick a variant from.

**Returns.** The chosen variant's id.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException` - `ingredient` is null.
- `InvalidOperationException` - The ingredient declares no variants, so there is nothing to draw.

### Render(Dimensions, IReadOnlyList&lt;PreviewLayer&gt;) { #m-render-nfty-core-model-dimensions-system-collections-g-7bf0b3 }

```csharp
public static Image<Rgba32> Render(Dimensions canvas, IReadOnlyList<PreviewLayer> bottomToTop);
```

Renders a stack of reference layers onto a transparent canvas.

**Parameters**

- `canvas` (`Dimensions`) - The output size. Every layer must match it exactly.
- `bottomToTop` (`IReadOnlyList<PreviewLayer>`) - The layers in paint order — index 0 paints first and everything after paints over it. An EMPTY list is legal and yields a fully transparent canvas: "no references on" is this feature's default state, not an error.

**Returns.** The composited preview. **The caller owns it** and must dispose it; every intermediate this method creates is disposed here, on the success path and on every failure path alike.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException` - `canvas` or `bottomToTop` is null.
- `ArgumentException` - A layer carries no ingredient. Reachable only through `default(PreviewLayer)` — a struct cannot enforce its own non-null field — which is why it is checked rather than assumed.
- `InvalidOperationException` - A layer's image does not match the canvas, or `VariantPreview.Render` refused it (unknown variant, colorized layer with no color).

### Split(RecipeManifest, string, IEnumerable&lt;string&gt;) { #m-split-nfty-core-model-recipemanifest-system-string-sys-adeafa }

```csharp
public static StackSplit Split(RecipeManifest recipe, string editedIngredientId, IEnumerable<string> enabledIngredientIds);
```

Splits a recipe's enabled reference layers around the layer being edited.

Ordering comes from [`LayerDepth`](Nfty.Core.Editing.LayerDepth.md) — the same 1-based, bottom-first projection of `layerOrder` that a layer table numbers its rows with — so the preview cannot disagree with the depths the author is looking at. It lives in Core precisely so the CLI and the GUI cannot compute the split two different ways.

**Parameters**

- `recipe` (`RecipeManifest`) - The recipe whose stack is being previewed.
- `editedIngredientId` (`string`) - The layer being authored. It is **pinned at its own depth** and never returned in either list, even if the caller also names it as enabled — it is the subject of the preview, not a reference in it.
- `enabledIngredientIds` (`IEnumerable<string>`) - Which reference layers the author has switched on. An id the recipe does not stack is IGNORED rather than rejected — it has no depth here, so there is no position to put it at — which keeps a stale checkbox left over from a removed layer out of the panel instead of throwing in the middle of a repaint. **This is not how a Kitchen layer gets placed.** Only ids the recipe stacks are ever returned, so passing a loose `.igt` id in here yields nothing at all. A Kitchen layer has no canonical depth by design, and the caller places it *in the gaps around* what this returns — entirely outside this method. An earlier version of this comment claimed the tolerance above WAS the Kitchen case; it is not, and a caller who believed it would silently drop every loose layer.

**Returns.** The enabled layers below and above, each bottom-to-top.

**Exceptions**

- `ArgumentNullException` - `recipe` or `enabledIngredientIds` is null.
- `KeyNotFoundException` - The recipe does not stack `editedIngredientId`. Unlike an unknown reference, this one has no sane reading: there is no depth to split around.
